REQ-28.generator_reply:

With ante = !h_re, the check is that h_rdata now equals its value one cycle earlier. In "next", ante is sampled on the previous edge, so it says that h_re was low at the previous edge. The cons is `h_rdata == $past(h_rdata)`, which compares the current value with the value at the previous edge.

This is slightly conservative: the read value may be updated in the cycle after h_re is high, since h_re high on the previous edge is exactly what the ante excludes. So the holding is stated only for cycles where h_re was low at the previous edge, and the update in the cycle right after h_re is not constrained.
